channel.title: AiGovOps Foundation — Latest from Ken & Bob
channel.description: The latest posts from Ken Johnston and Bob Rapp on AI governance, policy-as-code, and open-source compliance tooling.

item.title: The premise — Robodebt and the gate before the first notice
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: Australia's automated debt scheme averaged annual income into fortnights, fabricated debts for anyone with irregular earnings, and reversed the burden of proof onto about 440,000 people. The gate is not on the notice. It is on the arithmetic, before a single notice goes out. Level 400.

item.title: Seconds each — the hold that Cigna's PXDX never had
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: ProPublica reported that Cigna's PXDX process let medical directors deny large batches of claims in seconds each, often without opening the patient's file. The gate is a human who actually reviews before a denial — and the arithmetic of what "actually" means when the batch is a thousand deep. Level 300.

item.title: Forty-five minutes at Knight Capital — the deploy is the decision
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: In 2012 a faulty deploy sent $7 billion of unintended orders in 45 minutes and cost Knight Capital $440 million and the firm. No LLM anywhere. The gate it needed is the one your agent needs today: the deploy is a consequential action, and it gets a rule, a kill switch and a rehearsed way back.

item.title: The one-dollar Tahoe — why a system prompt is not a rule
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: In 2023 a dealer's chatbot agreed to sell a 2024 Chevy Tahoe for $1 and called it a legally binding offer. Nobody lost a truck. Everybody learned that a polite instruction to an LLM is not a gate. Level 200 starts here.

item.title: The café is open — say what brought you in, leave with a receipt
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: The Foundation's home page is a café now. Wren keeps the table by the door and asks one question. Five doors, each a real case; ten minutes to start; an hour to a rule in your own words, a signed receipt, and a Thursday.

item.title: The Fall 2026 Release — one hour to your first receipt, at whatever level you start
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: The Foundation's open-source projects become one practice with four levels, each an hour or less, each on a real case from the 100 verified harms — built on OVERT, the open standard from Glacis, which is the hero of this story.

item.title: The ten-minute Gate Check — is this AI agent ready to run?
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: Ten yes/no questions a manager can answer about an AI agent this week, each with the evidence to point at, ending in a card you keep. No account, no maybe.

item.title: ISO 42001 as controls you can run, not a binder you file
item.dc:creator: Bob Rapp
item.description: ISO 42001 is the AI management system standard. Treat its controls as checks you run in CI, each leaving a receipt an auditor can read, not a document you file.
